question:
(i) For an AC voltage applied to a pure resistor, obtain the relation between voltage and current and state the phase difference between them.
(ii) Compare this with the current obtained when the same AC voltage is applied across a semiconductor diode. Give reason for the difference.

options.A:
(i) In a pure resistor, $i=i_m\sin(\omega t-\pi/2)$, so current lags voltage by $\pi/2$.
(ii) A diode carries equal current in both AC half-cycles because it is an ohmic resistor.
options.B:
(i) If $v=v_m\sin\omega t$, then $i=\dfrac{v}{R}=i_m\sin\omega t$; current and voltage are in phase, so the phase difference is zero.
(ii) A semiconductor diode conducts appreciably only in its forward-biased half-cycle and has nearly zero current in reverse bias, unlike a resistor that conducts in both directions. This arises from one-way conduction of the p-n junction.
options.C:
(i) Current in a resistor leads voltage by $\pi/2$.
(ii) A diode has the same sinusoidal current in both halves as a resistor.
options.D:
(i) Current and voltage in a resistor are always $\pi$ out of phase.
(ii) A diode conducts only in reverse bias because its p-n junction blocks forward current.
